dct_description_sm:
This repository contains the protocol and supporting documentation used to harmonize SARS-CoV-2 serology data contributed by studies supported by the COVID-19 Immunity Task Force (CITF). The materials document the standardized variables, terminology, permissible values, assay metadata, harmonization-status classifications, and transformation rules applied in preparing the frozen CITF Databank release v1.0. Individual-level participant data are not included.

Harmonization protocol

The primary document is the CITF SARS-CoV-2 Serology Harmonization Protocol, version 2.8. It describes:

  • the scope of the serology harmonization process;
  • the target harmonized variables;
  • the mapping of study-specific variables to CITF Core Data Elements;
  • harmonization-status classifications;
  • the structure of the harmonized serology dataset;
  • data-quality and validation procedures; and
  • governance, access, and versioning requirements.

The repository also includes the CITF serology Core Data Element schema and supporting serological assay metadata. The reporting guide is included as source-data reporting guidance used by contributing studies.

Dataset structure

The harmonized serology dataset is organized at the result level. Each record represents one assay result for one participant. A participant may therefore have multiple records corresponding to different specimens, assays, or time points.

The target schema includes participant, specimen, and assay identifiers; specimen and assay characteristics; specimen-collection and assay dates; units of measurement; quantitative results; standardized binding antibody units where available; qualitative interpretations; assay measurement limits; and result-level quality-control indicators.

Harmonization and quality control

During harmonization, study-specific serology variables are mapped to the standardized CITF schema. Records are linked to standardized assay metadata using the CITF assay identifier. Quality-control procedures include:

  • validation of participant, specimen, and assay identifiers;
  • standardization and validation of dates, units, and categorical values;
  • review of assay metadata;
  • assessment of quantitative ranges;
  • duplicate-record detection; and
  • evaluation of internal consistency.

These procedures constitute dataset-level harmonization and quality control. They do not represent laboratory re-testing or independent biological validation of assay performance.

Scope limitations

Cell-mediated immunity data are outside the scope of this protocol and are not included in the harmonized serology dataset for Release v1.0. Neutralizing-antibody variables are also excluded from the harmonized dataset for this release.

Data access

Individual-level serology data are held under controlled access and are not included in this repository. Access to restricted data requires a formal request to the CITF Data Access Office and is subject to applicable institutional approvals, consent conditions, governance requirements, and data-sharing agreements.

Protocol version: 2.8
Databank release: v1.0
Release date: February 2026
